findings.message: member_base takes the newest record that has a PR URL and returns `conflict` when that PR is active with mergeStatus=conflicts. It does this before it looks at records[0].state. While the one conflict retry is running (record dispatched or running), the old PR still shows conflicts. Any later push to feature/<m> triggers `feature advance`, which sees `conflict` with fleet:conflict-retried already set, so it records `failed exit=merge-conflict` and adds fleet:refused. Fix: check whether the newest record is dispatched or running, and newer than the PR record, before reading the PR. If so, return `running`.
findings.scenario: Child 002-a conflicts and is retried with the merge ref, and its Job is running. Child 003-b's PR merges into feature/cat, which pushes to the branch and triggers advance. member_base(002-a) reads the old PR as `conflict`, finds the retried tag, and marks 002-a failed and refused while its retry Job is still running. Its dependents stay blocked.

findings.message: The `conflict` branch decides whether this is the retry by running `azdo_issue show | jq -e`. When `show` fails or returns junk, `jq -e` exits non-zero and the code takes the 'not yet retried' path. It tags fleet:conflict-retried and dispatches again with --force. 'Could not read the work item' is treated as 'tag absent'. Fix: capture the show output, check that it is an object, and count an unreadable item as an error (F_ERRORS++, skip) instead of retrying.
findings.scenario: Member 002-a has already used its retry and is still in conflict. A transient AzDO 5xx makes `azdo_issue show` fail. Advance treats the tag as missing and re-dispatches 002-a with --force, spending the assignee's plan on a second retry and bypassing the one-retry limit.

findings.message: When the PR read fails (`azdo_rest ... || out='{}'`), the jq verdict is `other` because targetRefName is null. member_base then falls through to the record, tag and consent checks. A member whose PR is really merged or in conflict is reported as `pending`/`ready` or `running`, never `?`. Fix: when a PR URL exists and the read fails or does not return an object, echo `?` and return.
findings.scenario: Child 002-a has a record with pr=.../pullrequest/11, and that PR is completed into feature/cat. AzDO answers 500 or the PAT lacks Code read. out is `{}`, so the state falls through to `pending` and then `ready`. Advance tries to re-dispatch an already merged child. Dependents and integration are held back while the output claims 'ready' instead of 'unknown'.
